question: A user wants to increase the durability and availability of data stored on an EBS volume. Which action could accomplish this?
explanation: Amazon EBS volumes are designed for an annual failure rate (AFR) of between 0.1% - 0.2%, where failure refers to a complete or partial loss of the volume, depending on the size and performance of the volume. This makes EBS volumes 20 times more reliable than typical commodity disk drives, which fail with an AFR of around 4%. For example, if you have 1,000 EBS volumes running for 1 year, you should expect 1 to 2 will have a failure. EBS also supports a snapshot feature, which is a good way to take point-in-time backups of your data. Reference: https://aws.amazon.com/ebs/details/
question_en: A user wants to increase the durability and availability of data stored on an EBS volume. Which action could accomplish this?
question_es: Un usuario desea aumentar la durabilidad y disponibilidad de los datos almacenados en un volumen de EBS. ¿Qué acción podría lograr esto?
explanation_en: Amazon EBS volumes are designed for an annual failure rate (AFR) of between 0.1% - 0.2%, where failure refers to a complete or partial loss of the volume, depending on the size and performance of the volume. This makes EBS volumes 20 times more reliable than typical commodity disk drives, which fail with an AFR of around 4%. For example, if you have 1,000 EBS volumes running for 1 year, you should expect 1 to 2 will have a failure. EBS also supports a snapshot feature, which is a good way to take point-in-time backups of your data. Reference: https://aws.amazon.com/ebs/details/
explanation_es: Los volúmenes de Amazon EBS están diseñados para una tasa de falla anual (AFR) de entre 0,1% y 0,2%, donde la falla se refiere a una pérdida total o parcial del volumen, según el tamaño y el rendimiento del volumen. Esto hace que los volúmenes de EBS sean 20 veces más confiables que las unidades de disco típicas, que fallan con un AFR de alrededor del 4%. Por ejemplo, si tiene 1000 volúmenes de EBS ejecutándose durante 1 año, debe esperar que 1 o 2 fallen. EBS también admite una función de instantáneas, que es una buena manera de realizar copias de seguridad de sus datos en un momento dado. Referencia: https://aws.amazon.com/ebs/details/

question: The billing process for Amazon EC2 instances was updated as of October 2, 2017. Which ofthe following statements is true regarding how you pay for Amazon EC2 instances? (Choose 2 answers) ​ You can pay for compute capacity by the hour only ​
options: You can pay per hour or per second, depending on the instance AMI's operating system
You can pay per hour or per second, depending on the instance type
You pay for compute capacity by the day; hours are billed in proportion
answer: You can pay per hour or per second, depending on the instance type
explanation: Previously, if you launched an instance for 5 minutes, you would pay for 1 hour. If you launched an instance for 45 minutes, you would also pay for 1 hour. This means that partial hours cost as much as one full hour. Pricing is per instance-hour consumed for each instance, from the time an instance is launched until it is terminated or stopped. Each partial instance- hour consumed will be billed as a full hour. With EC2 services now billed per-second in some cases, as well as per-hour in others as of October 2, 2017, there is more to consider. Amazon AWS is still based on the concept of pay- as-you-go. You pay Amazon EC2 instances by the second for all instance types except Dedicated Host, which is still billed per instance-hour. You are billed per second when using Linux operating systems with no separate hourly charge, and billed per hour when using Windows operating systems. Reference: http://aws.amazon.com/ec2/pricing/
question_en: The billing process for Amazon EC2 instances was updated as of October 2, 2017. Which ofthe following statements is true regarding how you pay for Amazon EC2 instances? (Choose 2 answers) ​ You can pay for compute capacity by the hour only ​
question_es: El proceso de facturación de las instancias de Amazon EC2 se actualizó el 2 de octubre de 2017. ¿Cuál de las siguientes afirmaciones es cierta con respecto a cómo se paga por las instancias de Amazon EC2? (Elija 2 respuestas) ​ Puede pagar por la capacidad de cómputo solo por hora ​
explanation_en: Previously, if you launched an instance for 5 minutes, you would pay for 1 hour. If you launched an instance for 45 minutes, you would also pay for 1 hour. This means that partial hours cost as much as one full hour. Pricing is per instance-hour consumed for each instance, from the time an instance is launched until it is terminated or stopped. Each partial instance- hour consumed will be billed as a full hour. With EC2 services now billed per-second in some cases, as well as per-hour in others as of October 2, 2017, there is more to consider. Amazon AWS is still based on the concept of pay- as-you-go. You pay Amazon EC2 instances by the second for all instance types except Dedicated Host, which is still billed per instance-hour. You are billed per second when using Linux operating systems with no separate hourly charge, and billed per hour when using Windows operating systems. Reference: http://aws.amazon.com/ec2/pricing/
explanation_es: Anteriormente, si lanzabas una instancia durante 5 minutos, pagabas por 1 hora. Si lanzaste una instancia durante 45 minutos, también pagarías 1 hora. Esto significa que las horas parciales cuestan tanto como una hora completa. El precio es por hora de instancia consumida para cada instancia, desde el momento en que se lanza una instancia hasta que finaliza o se detiene. Cada hora de instancia parcial consumida se facturará como una hora completa. Dado que los servicios EC2 ahora se facturan por segundo en algunos casos, así como por hora en otros a partir del 2 de octubre de 2017, hay más que considerar. Amazon AWS todavía se basa en el concepto de pago por uso. Usted paga las instancias de Amazon EC2 por segundo para todos los tipos de instancias, excepto para el host dedicado, que aún se factura por hora de instancia. Se le factura por segundo cuando utiliza sistemas operativos Linux sin cargo por hora separado, y se le factura por hora cuando utiliza sistemas operativos Windows. Referencia: http://aws.amazon.com/ec2/pricing/
options_es: Puedes pagar por hora o por segundo, dependiendo del sistema operativo de la AMI de la instancia
Puedes pagar por hora o por segundo, según el tipo de instancia
Paga por la capacidad informática por día; las horas se facturan en proporción

question: Which of the following statements is incorrect according to the policies of AWS regions?
options: The number of available Availability Zones are the same for all AWS regions
EC2 resources aren't replicated across AWS regions unless you do so specifically
Some EC2 resources might not be available in all AWS regions and Availability Zones.
Amazon EC2 provides you the ability to place resources, such as instances, and data in multiple locations
answer: The number of available Availability Zones are the same for all AWS regions
explanation: Amazon EC2 is hosted in multiple locations world-wide. These locations are composed of regions and Availability Zones. Each region is a separate geographic area. Each region has multiple, isolated locations known as Availability Zones. Amazon EC2 provides you the ability to place resources, such as instances, and data in multiple locations. Resources aren't replicated across regions unless you do so specifically. Reference: http://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/using-regions-availability-zones.ht ml

Each region has multiple, isolated locations known as Availability Zones. Amazon EC2 provides you the ability to place resources, such as instances, and data in multiple locations. Resources aren't replicated across regions unless you do so specifically. Reference: http://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/using-regions-availability-zones.ht ml
explanation_es: Amazon EC2 está alojado en varias ubicaciones en todo el mundo. Estas ubicaciones se componen de regiones y zonas de disponibilidad. Cada región es un área geográfica separada. Cada región tiene varias ubicaciones aisladas conocidas como zonas de disponibilidad. Amazon EC2 le brinda la posibilidad de colocar recursos, como instancias y datos, en varias ubicaciones. Los recursos no se replican entre regiones a menos que lo haga específicamente. Referencia: http://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/using-regions-availability-zones.ht ml

question: Unlike an IAM user, an IAM role _____ ​ is tightly tied to your accountÕs root credentials ​

question: Which of the four storage options involve data retrieval fees? (Choose 2 answers) ​ Amazon S3 Reduced Redundancy Storage ​ Amazon S3 Standard Storage ​
explanation: Amazon Glacier and S3 Standard-IA are both designed for storing infrequently accessed data. This is why the data storage fees are roughly one-half to one-sixth the cost of Standard Storage. Retrieval fees will quickly add up if the data is retrieved too often, so planning or correctly setting your object lifecycle based on how often you or your company will need the data is important. Reference: http://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/dev/storage-class-intro.html

explanation_en: Amazon Glacier and S3 Standard-IA are both designed for storing infrequently accessed data. This is why the data storage fees are roughly one-half to one-sixth the cost of Standard Storage. Retrieval fees will quickly add up if the data is retrieved too often, so planning or correctly setting your object lifecycle based on how often you or your company will need the data is important. Reference: http://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/dev/storage-class-intro.html
explanation_es: Amazon Glacier y S3 Standard-IA están diseñados para almacenar datos a los que se accede con poca frecuencia. Esta es la razón por la que las tarifas de almacenamiento de datos son aproximadamente entre la mitad y una sexta parte del costo del almacenamiento estándar. Las tarifas de recuperación se acumularán rápidamente si los datos se recuperan con demasiada frecuencia, por lo que es importante planificar o configurar correctamente el ciclo de vida de su objeto en función de la frecuencia con la que usted o su empresa necesitarán los datos. Referencia: http://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/dev/storage-class-intro.html

question: Which choice below is an advantage of using a Virtual Private Cloud (VPC)?

question: What statement about the On-Demand instances purchasing option provided by Amazon EC2 is correct?
options: You make a low, one-time, up-front payment for an instance, reserve it for a one- or three- year term, and pay a significantly lower rate for these instances
You specify the maximum per-minute price only that you are willing to pay to run a particular instance type
You pay only for the time you use instances, with no long-term commitments or up-front payments.
You make an all-front payment for an instance, reserve it for a one- or three-year term
answer: You pay only for the time you use instances, with no long-term commitments or up-front payments.
explanation: From 2006 until 2017, On-Demand instances allowed you to pay for the instances that you use by the hour, with no long-term commitments or up-front payments. In 2017, the payment policy was changed to include per-second billing, with a 1 minute minimum charge. The per-second billing option is only available for certain instance types and instanceoperating systems. Reference: https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/aws/new-per-second-billing-for-ec2-instances-and-ebs-volum es/
question_en: What statement about the On-Demand instances purchasing option provided by Amazon EC2 is correct?
question_es: ¿Qué afirmación es correcta sobre la opción de compra de instancias bajo demanda proporcionada por Amazon EC2?
explanation_en: From 2006 until 2017, On-Demand instances allowed you to pay for the instances that you use by the hour, with no long-term commitments or up-front payments. In 2017, the payment policy was changed to include per-second billing, with a 1 minute minimum charge. The per-second billing option is only available for certain instance types and instanceoperating systems. Reference: https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/aws/new-per-second-billing-for-ec2-instances-and-ebs-volum es/
explanation_es: Desde 2006 hasta 2017, las instancias On-Demand le permitían pagar las instancias que usaba por horas, sin compromisos a largo plazo ni pagos por adelantado. En 2017 se cambió la política de pago para incluir facturación por segundo, con un cargo mínimo de 1 minuto. La opción de facturación por segundo solo está disponible para ciertos tipos de instancias y sistemas operativos de instancias. Referencia: https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/aws/new-per- second-billing-for-ec2-instances-and-ebs-volum es/

question: If your AWS data must meet specific regulations such as the EU Data protection laws, what must you do?
options: Keep that data on-premise and do not move it to the cloud under any circumstance
Architect your environment to meet these security requirements
Move your data somewhere else so you donÕt have to worry about extra security
Be aware that they exist and comply to them when and if you have time to do so
answer: Architect your environment to meet these security requirements
explanation: Some laws require specific security controls, retention requirements, etc, dependent on the data being stored. Other legislations exist where certain data may have to remain within a specific region and can not be transferred out of those boundaries. You need to architect your environment to meet these security requirement and mitigate the risk of data being stored in a geographic location thatÕs restricted. Breaches to this legislation could have a legal impact and lead to additional risks against your organization, so it's fundamental that you are aware of your data privacy and storage location laws and regulations.

question: You have been asked to perform some penetration testing on your company's AWS infrastructure. However you are not sure who is responsible for this, your company or AWS? Which statements correctly describe the AWS policy in relation to penetration testing? (Choose 2 answers) ​
options: The information you share with AWS as part of this process is kept confidential within AWS
You need to employ a 3rd party specialist to do the testing
You can do the testing with no prior AWS approval
Permission is required from AWS for all penetration testing
answer: Permission is required from AWS for all penetration testing
explanation: There are several important things to note about penetration testing requests: . Permission is required for all penetration tests. . To request permission, you must be logged into the AWS portal using the root credentials associated with the instances you wish to test, otherwise the form will not pre-populate correctly. . The AWS policy only permits testing of EC2 and RDS instances that you own. Tests against any other AWS services or AWS-owned resources are prohibited . At this time, the AWS policy does not permit testing small or micro RDS instance types. Testing of m1.small, t1.micro or t2.nano EC2 instance types is not permitted. Reference: http://aws.amazon.com/security/penetration-testing/

The AWS policy only permits testing of EC2 and RDS instances that you own. Tests against any other AWS services or AWS-owned resources are prohibited . At this time, the AWS policy does not permit testing small or micro RDS instance types. Testing of m1.small, t1.micro or t2.nano EC2 instance types is not permitted. Reference: http://aws.amazon.com/security/penetration-testing/
explanation_es: Hay varias cosas importantes a tener en cuenta acerca de las solicitudes de pruebas de penetración: . Se requiere permiso para todas las pruebas de penetración. . Para solicitar permiso, debe iniciar sesión en el portal de AWS utilizando las credenciales raíz asociadas con las instancias que desea probar; de lo contrario, el formulario no se completará correctamente. . La política de AWS solo permite probar instancias EC2 y RDS de su propiedad. Están prohibidas las pruebas con otros servicios de AWS o recursos propiedad de AWS. En este momento, la política de AWS no permite probar tipos de instancias RDS pequeñas o micro. No se permiten pruebas de los tipos de instancia EC2 m1.small, t1.micro o t2.nano. Referencia: http://aws.amazon.com/security/penetration-testing/

question: Amazon ______ provides durable, block-level storage volumes you can attach to a running instance and which persist beyond the ​ Elastic File System ​
explanation: Amazon EBS provides durable, block-level storage volumes that you can attach to a running instance. You can use Amazon EBS as a primary storage device for data that requires frequent and granular updates. For example, Amazon EBS is the recommended storage option when you run a database on an instance. An EBS volume behaves like a raw, unformatted, external block device that you can attach to a single instance. The volume persists independently from the running life of an instance. Reference: http://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/Storage.html

question: Which of the following is an AWS security best practice?

question: Which statement is correct about AWS Key Management Service (KMS)?
options: KMS is a managed service from AWS that enables you to easily manage and maintain encryption Keys.
KMS is a managed service from AWS that can help you generate Key-Pairs to use for instance authentication
KMS is a managed service from AWS that provides Encryption-as-a-service to data at rest
KMS is an Identity and Access Management (IAM) service that helps you generate SSH keys for IAM users to use for Authentication instead of passwords
answer: KMS is a managed service from AWS that enables you to easily manage and maintain encryption Keys.
explanation: Key Management Service is a software as a service offering from Amazon. It is a managed service provided by Amazon that enables you to easily manage encryption keys. Administrators at Amazon do not have access to your keys. They cannot recover your keys and they do not help you with encryption of your keys. AWS simply administers the operating system and the underlying application it's up to us to administer our encryption keys and administer how those keys are used.
question_en: Which statement is correct about AWS Key Management Service (KMS)?
question_es: ¿Qué afirmación es correcta sobre AWS Key Management Service (KMS)?
explanation_en: Key Management Service is a software as a service offering from Amazon. It is a managed service provided by Amazon that enables you to easily manage encryption keys. Administrators at Amazon do not have access to your keys. They cannot recover your keys and they do not help you with encryption of your keys. AWS simply administers the operating system and the underlying application it's up to us to administer our encryption keys and administer how those keys are used.
explanation_es: Key Management Service es una oferta de software como servicio de Amazon. Es un servicio administrado proporcionado por Amazon que le permite administrar fácilmente claves de cifrado. Los administradores de Amazon no tienen acceso a sus claves. No pueden recuperar sus claves y no le ayudan con el cifrado de sus claves. AWS simplemente administra el sistema operativo y la aplicación subyacente. Depende de nosotros administrar nuestras claves de cifrado y administrar cómo se utilizan esas claves.
options_es: KMS es un servicio administrado de AWS que le permite administrar y mantener claves de cifrado fácilmente.
KMS es un servicio administrado de AWS que puede ayudarlo a generar pares de claves para usar, por ejemplo, autenticación
KMS es un servicio administrado de AWS que proporciona cifrado como servicio a datos en reposo
KMS es un servicio de administración de identidad y acceso (IAM) que le ayuda a generar claves SSH para que los usuarios de IAM las utilicen para la autenticación en lugar de contraseñas.

question: A user is uploading a backup of data to Glacier for the purpose of Disaster Recovery(DR). The data may be required to restore only when there is DR and the organization is planning RTO of 1 hour. What advise will you provide to the user?
options: This is not the right case for Glacier; instead use S3
Use the Glacier SDK to upload data directly from EC2 to Glacier
Use the Glacier CLIs to upload data from EC2 to Glacier
Use the Glacier console to upload data to Glacier
answer: This is not the right case for Glacier; instead use S3
explanation: AWS Glacier is a long term cheaper archival service which is used for infrequent user storage. In this case since RTO is 1 hour, Glacier will not meet the requirement as it takes 3-5 hours to make the data available. In this case it is recommended to store content in S3/RRS. Reference: http://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazonglacier/latest/dev/introduction.html

In this case since RTO is 1 hour, Glacier will not meet the requirement as it takes 3-5 hours to make the data available. In this case it is recommended to store content in S3/RRS. Reference: http://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazonglacier/latest/dev/introduction.html
explanation_es: AWS Glacier es un servicio de archivo más económico a largo plazo que se utiliza para el almacenamiento de usuarios poco frecuentes. En este caso se recomienda almacenar el contenido en S3/RRS. Referencia: http://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazonglacier/latest/dev/introduction.html

question: Which of the following is true of Amazon CloudWatch?
options: Amazon CloudWatch monitors Amazon Web Services (AWS) resources and the applications that run on AWS in real-time
Amazon CloudWatch runs code without provisioning or managing servers
Amazon CloudWatch is a web service that gives businesses an easy and cost effective way to distribute content with low latency and high data transfer speeds.
answer: Amazon CloudWatch monitors Amazon Web Services (AWS) resources and the applications that run on AWS in real-time
explanation: Amazon CloudWatch monitors your Amazon Web Services (AWS) resources and the applications you run on AWS in real-time. You can use CloudWatch to collect and track metrics, which are variables you can measure for your resources and applications. CloudWatch alarms send notifications or automatically make changes to the resources you are monitoring based on rules that you define. For example, you can monitor the CPU usage and disk reads and writes of your Amazon EC2 instances and then use this data to determine whether you should launch additional instances to handle increased load. You can also use this data to stop under-used instances to save money. In addition to monitoring the built-in metrics that come with AWS, you can monitor your own custom metrics. With CloudWatch, you gain system-wide visibility into resource utilization, application performance, and operational health. Reference: http://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/DeveloperGuide/WhatIsCloudWatc h.html

question: A recovery time objective (RTO) is related to _______, while a recovery point objective (RPO) is related to _______. ​ data loss measured in time; time required for system restoration ​
options: time required for system restoration; data loss measured in time
the actual time for a system to restore; the estimated time for a system to restore
the estimated time for a system to restore; the actual time for a system to restore
answer: time required for system restoration; data loss measured in time
explanation: A recovery time objective (RTO) is the time it takes to restore system service after a disruption, while a recovery point objective (RPO) is an acceptable amount of data loss measured in time. The two concepts are interrelated. The amount of data loss a business can tolerate usually determines the desired recovery time objective. The desired RTO then generally determines the disaster recovery method. Reference: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Recovery_point_objective
question_en: A recovery time objective (RTO) is related to _______, while a recovery point objective (RPO) is related to _______. ​ data loss measured in time; time required for system restoration ​
question_es: Un objetivo de tiempo de recuperación (RTO) está relacionado con _______, mientras que un objetivo de punto de recuperación (RPO) está relacionado con _______. ​ pérdida de datos medida en el tiempo; tiempo necesario para la restauración del sistema
explanation_en: A recovery time objective (RTO) is the time it takes to restore system service after a disruption, while a recovery point objective (RPO) is an acceptable amount of data loss measured in time. The two concepts are interrelated. The amount of data loss a business can tolerate usually determines the desired recovery time objective. The desired RTO then generally determines the disaster recovery method. Reference: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Recovery_point_objective
explanation_es: Un objetivo de tiempo de recuperación (RTO) es el tiempo que lleva restaurar el servicio del sistema después de una interrupción, mientras que un objetivo de punto de recuperación (RPO) es una cantidad aceptable de pérdida de datos medida en el tiempo. Los dos conceptos están interrelacionados. La cantidad de pérdida de datos que una empresa puede tolerar suele determinar el objetivo de tiempo de recuperación deseado. El RTO deseado generalmente determina el método de recuperación ante desastres. Referencia: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Recovery_point_objective

el tiempo real para que un sistema se restaure; el tiempo estimado para que un sistema se restaure

question: A user has developed an application that requires sending data to a NoSQL database. The user wants to decouple the process so that the application keeps processing and sending data, but does not wait for database acknowledgement. Which of the below mentioned applications helps in this scenario?
explanation: SQS provides a simple and cost-effective way to decouple the components of an application. In this case, the user can use AWS SQS to send messages which are received from an application and sent to DB. The application can continue processing data without waiting for any acknowledgement from DB. The user can use SQS to transmit any volume of data without losing messages or requiring other services to always be available. While SNS is a messaging service, it does not offer the specific decoupling necessary in this case. Reference: http://aws.amazon.com/sqs/

question: The process of authentication can be categorised into two distinct parts of information, these being:
explanation: The first part of this process is to define who you are, effectively presenting your identity, an example of this would be your login username to your AWS account or environment. This identification is a unique value within the system that you are trying to authenticate to, and in this example, AWS would not allow 2 identical user accounts to be created within the same single AWS Account. The second part of the authentication process is to verify that you are who you say you are in the first step. This is achieved by providing additional information, which should be kept private and secret for security purposes, however this private information does not have to be a unique value within the system. So in the example I just gave, whereby you provide your identity in the form of a username to your AWS Account, which will be a unique value, the next step would be to verify that identity by providing a password.

question: Pricing is ____ consumed for EC2 instances ​

explanation: In AWS, you pay only for what you use. EC2 pricing is per instance-second consumed, or per instance-hour consumed depending on the instance type and operating system for the AMI. question: You are implementing Amazon CloudWatch for monitoring of your AWS infrastructure. What can you use within CloudWatch to take actions such as sending a notification to an SNS topic or an Auto Scaling policy?
explanation: You can use an alarm to automatically initiate actions on your behalf. An alarm watches a single metric over a specified time period, and performs one or more specified actions, based on the value of the metric relative to a threshold over time. Alarms invoke actions for sustained state changes only. CloudWatch alarms will not invoke actions simply because they are in a particular state. The state must have changed and been maintained for a specified number of periods. Reference: http://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/cloudwatch_concepts.h tm

question: What two options does RDS offer to backup information stored on DB instances? (Choose 2 answers) ​
explanation: The two methods for backing up information stored on RDS DB instances are automated backups and DB snapshots. Automated backup is a managed process where RDS creates standby instances of any and all instances selected for Multi-Availability Zone (AZ) deployment rather than Single AZ deployment. DB snapshots are also copies of the DB instance, but snapshots are manual processes, and snapshots can be stored in availability zones or regions selected by the user. DB versioning is not a method of backing up RDS DB instances. Versioning is a method for backing up objects stored in S3. DB read replicas are not a method of backing up RDS DB instances. Read replicas allow databases to manage a level of read requests for a database that extends beyond an individual DB instance's capability. Reference: http://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_WorkingWithAutomated Backups.html
question_en: What two options does RDS offer to backup information stored on DB instances? (Choose 2 answers) ​
question_es: ¿Qué dos opciones ofrece RDS para realizar copias de seguridad de la información almacenada en instancias de base de datos? (Elija 2 respuestas) ​
explanation_en: The two methods for backing up information stored on RDS DB instances are automated backups and DB snapshots. Automated backup is a managed process where RDS creates standby instances of any and all instances selected for Multi-Availability Zone (AZ) deployment rather than Single AZ deployment. DB snapshots are also copies of the DB instance, but snapshots are manual processes, and snapshots can be stored in availability zones or regions selected by the user. DB versioning is not a method of backing up RDS DB instances. Versioning is a method for backing up objects stored in S3. DB read replicas are not a method of backing up RDS DB instances. Read replicas allow databases to manage a level of read requests for a database that extends beyond an individual DB instance's capability. Reference: http://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_WorkingWithAutomated Backups.html
explanation_es: Los dos métodos para realizar copias de seguridad de la información almacenada en instancias de base de datos de RDS son las copias de seguridad automatizadas y las instantáneas de bases de datos. La copia de seguridad automatizada es un proceso administrado en el que RDS crea instancias en espera de todas y cada una de las instancias seleccionadas para la implementación de zona de disponibilidad múltiple (AZ) en lugar de la implementación de una sola AZ. Las instantáneas de base de datos también son copias de la instancia de base de datos, pero son procesos manuales y se pueden almacenar en zonas o regiones de disponibilidad seleccionadas por el usuario. El control de versiones de bases de datos no es un método para realizar copias de seguridad de instancias de bases de datos RDS. El control de versiones es un método para realizar copias de seguridad de objetos almacenados en S3. Las réplicas de lectura de base de datos no son un método para realizar copias de seguridad de instancias de base de datos RDS. question: Why does AWS recommend that you locate your ElastiCache clusters or nodes in different Availability Zones?
options: To eliminate the chance that a single AZ failure will cause your entire system to fail
To enable one Availability Zone to provide a lower latency than the other
To improve the scalability of the system
To be able to configure load balancing
answer: To eliminate the chance that a single AZ failure will cause your entire system to fail
explanation: AWS recommends that you locate your ElastiCache clusters or nodes in different Availability Zones to eliminate the chance that a failure will cause your entire system to fail. question: In S3, what is a key for an object?
options: A secure ID to decrypt the object content
A secure ID to download the object
A unique identifier of an object to identify it within a bucket
A key to securely access the S3 object
answer: A unique identifier of an object to identify it within a bucket
explanation: A key is a unique identifier for an object within a bucket. It makes the combination of bucket + key + version ID to uniquely identify the object. Every object in Amazon S3 can be uniquely identified with the help of the web service endpoint (region specific), bucket name (unique across S3), key (A unique identifier) and optionally, a version. For example, in theURL: http://mydatatest.s3.amazonaws.com/2014-03-01/AmazonS3.jpg "mydatatest" is the name of the bucket and "2014-03-01/AmazonS3.jpg" is the key to identify the object "AmazonS3.jpg". Reference: http://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/dev/Introduction.html
question_en: In S3, what is a key for an object?
question_es: En S3, ¿qué es una clave para un objeto?
explanation_en: A key is a unique identifier for an object within a bucket. It makes the combination of bucket + key + version ID to uniquely identify the object. Every object in Amazon S3 can be uniquely identified with the help of the web service endpoint (region specific), bucket name (unique across S3), key (A unique identifier) and optionally, a version. For example, in theURL: http://mydatatest.s3.amazonaws.com/2014-03-01/AmazonS3.jpg "mydatatest" is the name of the bucket and "2014-03-01/AmazonS3.jpg" is the key to identify the object "AmazonS3.jpg". Reference: http://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/dev/Introduction.html
explanation_es: Una clave es un identificador único para un objeto dentro de un depósito. Realiza la combinación de depósito + clave + ID de versión para identificar de forma única el objeto. Cada objeto en Amazon S3 se puede identificar de forma única con la ayuda del punto final del servicio web (específico de la región), el nombre del depósito (único en S3), la clave (un identificador único) y, opcionalmente, una versión. Por ejemplo, en la URL: http://mydatatest.s3.amazonaws.com/2014-03-01/AmazonS3.jpg "mydatatest" es el nombre del depósito y "2014-03-01/AmazonS3.jpg" es la clave para identificar el objeto "AmazonS3.jpg". Referencia: http://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/dev/Introduction.html

question: If you didn't set the tenancy of an instance to when you launched it into your VPC, you must stop the running instance, set the tenancy, and relaunch it. ​ default ​
explanation: Dedicated instances are Amazon EC2 instances that run in a virtual private cloud (VPC) on hardware that's dedicated to a single customer. Each instance that you launch into a VPC has a tenancy attribute. This attribute can be either a default type, or a dedicated type, or a host type. You cannot change the tenancy of a default instance after you've launched it. You can change the tenancy of an instance from dedicated to host after you've launched it, and vice versa. To change the tenancy of an instance, you have to select your instance, stop it, modify your instance, and then choose whether to run your instance on dedicated hardware or on a Dedicated Host. question: Which of the choices below best describes what Auto Scaling is well suited for?
options: only for applications that experience hourly, daily, or weekly variability in usage

only for applications with a stable usage pattern but extremely high workload
Both for applications that use frameworks and SDKs to enhance its customer relationship
answer: Both for applications that have stable demand patterns and that experience hourly, daily, or weekly variability in usage.
explanation: Auto Scaling is well suited to both applications that have stable demand patterns and that experience hourly, daily, or weekly variability in usage. Whether the demand is predictable or unpredictable auto scaling can be a good choice. If the demand is predictable and long term you may choose reserved instances. If the demand is unpredictable you may choose on-demand or even spot instance (if you can afford to have an instance lost unexpectedly). Reference: http://aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/

question: A user has launched an EBS backed EC2 instance with a Windows operating system. Which statement below is accurate regarding how instances are billed when rebooted or stopped and restarted?
options: Every reboot is charged by AWS as a separate hour, while multiple start/stop actionsduring a single hour will be counted as a single hour.
For rebooting AWS does not charge a new instance hour, while every stop or restart will be charged fee for a new instance hour as a separate hour
For every reboot or start/stop, the user will be charged as a separate hour
For rebooting AWS charges extra only once, while for every stop/start the user will be charged as a separate hour
answer: For rebooting AWS does not charge a new instance hour, while every stop or restart will be charged fee for a new instance hour as a separate hour
explanation: For an EC2 instance launched with an EBS backed Windows AMI, each time the instance state is changed from stop to start/ running, AWS charges restart a new per-hour charge. Effective October 2, 2017, charges are calculated on a per-second basis for On-Demand, Spot and Reserved instances with Linux operating systems, with a minimum one-minute charge. Regardless of operating system, rebooting an instance AWS does not incur a charge an hour or one-minute minimum charge. Reference: http://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/ec2-instance-lifecycle.html
question_en: A user has launched an EBS backed EC2 instance with a Windows operating system. Which statement below is accurate regarding how instances are billed when rebooted or stopped and restarted?

explanation_en: For an EC2 instance launched with an EBS backed Windows AMI, each time the instance state is changed from stop to start/ running, AWS charges restart a new per-hour charge. Regardless of operating system, rebooting an instance AWS does not incur a charge an hour or one-minute minimum charge. Reference: http://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/ec2-instance-lifecycle.html
explanation_es: Para una instancia EC2 lanzada con una AMI de Windows respaldada por EBS, cada vez que el estado de la instancia cambia de parada a inicio/ejecución, AWS cobra un nuevo cargo por hora. A partir del 2 de octubre de 2017, los cargos se calculan por segundo para instancias bajo demanda, puntuales y reservadas con sistemas operativos Linux, con un cargo mínimo de un minuto. Independientemente del sistema operativo, reiniciar una instancia de AWS no genera un cargo mínimo por hora o por minuto. Referencia: http://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/ec2-instance-lifecycle.html

question: Which statement is FALSE relating to IAM Groups?

answer: IAM Groups are used for authentication
explanation: IAM Groups are objects much like user objects, however they are not used in any authentication process, but they are used to authorise access to AWS resources through the use of AWS Policies. IAM Groups contain IAM Users, and these groups will have IAM policies associated that will allow or explicitly deny access to AWS resources. These policies are either AWS Managed policies that can be selected from within IAM, or customer managed policies that are created by you, the customer. More information on IAM Policies will be discussed in a lecture devoted to this element. question: Which of the following statements best describes a key difference between Elastic Beanstalk and CloudFormation?
options: Elastic Beanstalk uses Elastic load balancing and CloudFormation doesn't
CloudFormation is faster in deploying applications than Elastic Beanstalk
Elastic Beanstalk is faster in deploying applications than CloudFormation.
CloudFormation offers more potential for customization than Elastic Beanstalk, because you can actually design and script yourself
answer: CloudFormation offers more potential for customization than Elastic Beanstalk, because you can actually design and script yourself
explanation: These services are designed to complement each other. AWS Elastic Beanstalk provides an environment to easily develop and run applications in the cloud. It is integrated with developer tools and provides a one-stop experience for you to manage the lifecycle of your applications. AWS CloudFormation is a convenient deployment mechanism for a broad rangeof AWS resources. It supports the infrastructure needs of many different types of applications such as existing enterprise applications, legacy applications, applications built using a variety of AWS resources and container-based solutions (including those built using AWS Elastic Beanstalk). AWS CloudFormation introduces two new concepts: The template, a JSON-format, text-based file that describes all the AWS resources you need to deploy to run your application and the stack, the set of AWS resources that are created and managed as a single unit when AWS CloudFormation instantiates a template. Reference: http://aws.amazon.com/cloudformation/faqs/
question_en: Which of the following statements best describes a key difference between Elastic Beanstalk and CloudFormation?
question_es: ¿Cuál de las siguientes afirmaciones describe mejor una diferencia clave entre Elastic Beanstalk y CloudFormation?
explanation_en: These services are designed to complement each other. AWS Elastic Beanstalk provides an environment to easily develop and run applications in the cloud. It is integrated with developer tools and provides a one-stop experience for you to manage the lifecycle of your applications. AWS CloudFormation is a convenient deployment mechanism for a broad rangeof AWS resources. It supports the infrastructure needs of many different types of applications such as existing enterprise applications, legacy applications, applications built using a variety of AWS resources and container-based solutions (including those built using AWS Elastic Beanstalk). AWS CloudFormation introduces two new concepts: The template, a JSON-format, text-based file that describes all the AWS resources you need to deploy to run your application and the stack, the set of AWS resources that are created and managed as a single unit when AWS CloudFormation instantiates a template. Reference: http://aws.amazon.com/cloudformation/faqs/
explanation_es: Estos servicios están diseñados para complementarse entre sí. AWS Elastic Beanstalk proporciona un entorno para desarrollar y ejecutar aplicaciones en la nube fácilmente. Está integrado con herramientas de desarrollador y proporciona una experiencia integral para que usted administre el ciclo de vida de sus aplicaciones. AWS CloudFormation es un mecanismo de implementación conveniente para una amplia gama de recursos de AWS. Admite las necesidades de infraestructura de muchos tipos diferentes de aplicaciones, como aplicaciones empresariales existentes, aplicaciones heredadas, aplicaciones creadas con una variedad de recursos de AWS y soluciones basadas en contenedores (incluidas las creadas con AWS Elastic Beanstalk). AWS CloudFormation presenta dos conceptos nuevos: la plantilla, un archivo basado en texto en formato JSON que describe todos los recursos de AWS que necesita implementar para ejecutar su aplicación y la pila, el conjunto de recursos de AWS que se crean y administran como una sola unidad cuando AWS CloudFormation crea una instancia de una plantilla. question: If you have two EC2 instances in different regions, how will you be charged for data transfer?

question: An organization has setup consolidated billing with 3 different AWS accounts. Which of the below mentioned advantages will organization receive in terms of the AWS pricing?
options: The EC2 instances of each account will receive a total of 750*3 micro instance hours free
The free usage tier for all the 3 accounts will be 3 years and not a single year
The consolidated billing does not bring any cost advantage for the organization
lower prices for services where volume pricing tiers are available
answer: lower prices for services where volume pricing tiers are available
explanation: For billing purposes, AWS treats all the accounts in the organization as if they were one account. Some services, such as Amazon EC2 and Amazon S3, have volume pricing tiers across certain usage dimensions that give you lower prices the more you use the service. With consolidated billing, AWS combines the usage from all accounts to determine which volume pricing tiers to apply, giving you a lower overall price whenever possible. AWS then allocates each member account a portion of the overall volume discount based on the account's usage. Reference: http://docs.aws.amazon.com/awsaccountbilling/latest/about/consolidatedbilling.html

AWS then allocates each member account a portion of the overall volume discount based on the account's usage. Reference: http://docs.aws.amazon.com/awsaccountbilling/latest/about/consolidatedbilling.html
explanation_es: A efectos de facturación, AWS trata todas las cuentas de la organización como si fueran una sola. Algunos servicios, como Amazon EC2 y Amazon S3, tienen niveles de precios por volumen en determinadas dimensiones de uso que le ofrecen precios más bajos cuanto más utiliza el servicio. Con la facturación consolidada, AWS combina el uso de todas las cuentas para determinar qué niveles de precios por volumen aplicar, ofreciéndole un precio general más bajo siempre que sea posible. Luego, AWS asigna a cada cuenta miembro una parte del descuento por volumen general en función del uso de la cuenta. question: In S3, which of the following refers to object metadata?
options: A set of name-value pairs that describe an object
A meta model of a bucket that is inherited by an object
An auto generated key and it's corresponding value
A unique identifier of an object name within a bucket
answer: A set of name-value pairs that describe an object
explanation: Each of the S3 objects consists of object data and metadata. The data portion is opaque to Amazon S3. The metadata is a set of name-value pairs that describe the object. The metadata distinguishes the object from a regular file as it is additional information storedalong with the object data. The metadata can be the object name, version ID, created date, Content- Type, and also some more user-defined attributes. Reference: http://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/dev/Introduction.html
question_en: In S3, which of the following refers to object metadata?
question_es: En S3, ¿cuál de las siguientes opciones se refiere a metadatos de objetos?
explanation_en: Each of the S3 objects consists of object data and metadata. The data portion is opaque to Amazon S3. The metadata is a set of name-value pairs that describe the object. The metadata distinguishes the object from a regular file as it is additional information storedalong with the object data. The metadata can be the object name, version ID, created date, Content- Type, and also some more user-defined attributes. Reference: http://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/dev/Introduction.html
explanation_es: Cada uno de los objetos de S3 consta de datos y metadatos de objetos. La parte de datos es opaca para Amazon S3. Los metadatos son un conjunto de pares nombre-valor que describen el objeto. Los metadatos distinguen el objeto de un archivo normal, ya que es información adicional almacenada junto con los datos del objeto. Los metadatos pueden ser el nombre del objeto, el ID de la versión, la fecha de creación, el tipo de contenido y también algunos atributos más definidos por el usuario. Referencia: http://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/dev/Introduction.html
options_es: Un conjunto de pares nombre-valor que describen un objeto

Una clave generada automáticamente y su valor correspondiente
Un identificador único de un nombre de objeto dentro de un depósito.

question: You are launching an Amazon EC2 instance and need to decide which instance type is best for your application. You see that Amazon recommends using their current generation types for the best performance. Which instance family is only offered in the previous generation of instance types?
explanation: Amazon Web Services offers previous generation instances for users who have optimized their applications around these instances and have yet to upgrade. AWS supports these previous generation instances, but recommends that you use the latest generation of instances to get the best performance. Micro instances have low network performance and storage capacity and are no longer offered as a current generation instance type. There are micro instances still available - the t2.micro instance is available as part of the general purpose instance family, but Micro instances are no longer their own separate family. Reference: http://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/instance-types.html

Micro instances have low network performance and storage capacity and are no longer offered as a current generation instance type. There are micro instances still available - the t2.micro instance is available as part of the general purpose instance family, but Micro instances are no longer their own separate family. Reference: http://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/instance-types.html
explanation_es: Amazon Web Services ofrece instancias de generación anterior para usuarios que han optimizado sus aplicaciones en torno a estas instancias y aún no han actualizado. AWS admite estas instancias de la generación anterior, pero recomienda utilizar la última generación de instancias para obtener el mejor rendimiento. Las microinstancias tienen un rendimiento de red y una capacidad de almacenamiento bajos y ya no se ofrecen como tipo de instancia de la generación actual. Todavía hay microinstancias disponibles: la instancia t2.micro está disponible como parte de la familia de instancias de uso general, pero las microinstancias ya no son una familia separada. question: A user has launched an EBS optimized instance with EC2. Which of the below mentioned options is the correct statement?
options: It provides additional dedicated capacity for EBS IO
The attached EBS will have greater storage capacity
The user will have a PIOPS based EBS volume
It will be launched on dedicated hardware in VPC
answer: It provides additional dedicated capacity for EBS IO
explanation: An Amazon EBS-optimized instance uses an optimized configuration stack and provides additional, dedicated capacity for the Amazon EBS I/O. This optimization provides the best performance for the userÕs Amazon EBS volumes by minimizing contention between the Amazon EBS I/O and other traffic from the userÕs instance. Reference: http://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/EBSOptimized.html
question_en: A user has launched an EBS optimized instance with EC2. Which of the below mentioned options is the correct statement?

This optimization provides the best performance for the userÕs Amazon EBS volumes by minimizing contention between the Amazon EBS I/O and other traffic from the userÕs instance. Reference: http://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/EBSOptimized.html
explanation_es: Una instancia optimizada para Amazon EBS utiliza una pila de configuración optimizada y proporciona capacidad dedicada adicional para la E/S de Amazon EBS. Esta optimización proporciona el mejor rendimiento para los volúmenes de Amazon EBS del usuario al minimizar la contención entre la E/S de Amazon EBS y otro tráfico de la instancia del usuario. question: In S3, what is the basic difference between a file and an object?
explanation: A file can be a video, a text file, or a photo for example. An object is a file of any kind plus metadata to organize it. When a user uploads a file from the specified folder to the S3 bucket, S3 assigns a key value that is a combination of the uploaded file name. If the user has specified a folder name the key will have the folder name as a prefix. Reference: http://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/UG/UploadingObjectsintoAmazonS3.html
question_en: In S3, what is the basic difference between a file and an object?
question_es: En S3, ¿cuál es la diferencia básica entre un archivo y un objeto?
explanation_en: A file can be a video, a text file, or a photo for example. An object is a file of any kind plus metadata to organize it. When a user uploads a file from the specified folder to the S3 bucket, S3 assigns a key value that is a combination of the uploaded file name. If the user has specified a folder name the key will have the folder name as a prefix. Reference: http://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/UG/UploadingObjectsintoAmazonS3.html
explanation_es: Un archivo puede ser un vídeo, un archivo de texto o una foto, por ejemplo. Un objeto es un archivo de cualquier tipo más metadatos para organizarlo. Cuando un usuario carga un archivo desde la carpeta especificada al depósito de S3, S3 asigna un valor clave que es una combinación del nombre del archivo cargado. Si el usuario ha especificado un nombre de carpeta, la clave tendrá el nombre de la carpeta como prefijo. Referencia: http://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/UG/UploadingObjectsintoAmazonS3.html
